# requireDouble

<link-summary>Returns the value as a number with a fractional part, or throws.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireDouble() — Returns the value as a number with a fractional part, or throws. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireDouble(
  value: unknown,
  message: string = "Expected a number with a fractional part."
): number;
```

A synonym of the `Float` family, offered under the name people reach for first. In JavaScript every number already is a double, so `double` names no runtime distinction of its own.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter                                                              | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :--------------------------------------------------------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `value`                                                                | `unknown` | The value to validate.                                        |
| `message` _(optional)_ `= "Expected a number with a fractional part."` | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`number` — the same value, typed as a number with a fractional part.

## Throws

| Exception                  | Condition                                         |
| :------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------ |
| `IllegalArgumentException` | the value is not a number with a fractional part. |

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
requireDouble(1.5); // => 1.5
requireDouble(-0.1); // => -0.1
requireDouble(42); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireDouble(1.0); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
